## Executive Summary

MinecraftForge is the two-decade patriarch of Minecraft modding and the codebase NeoForge
forked in 2023. Analyzed comparatively: the modern FML architecture is documented in the
fancymodloader dossier; what this baseline uniquely shows is (1) the **pre-consolidation
layout** — fmlloader/fmlcore/fmlearlydisplay plus language providers as separate subprojects
(javafmllanguage, lowcodelanguage, mclanguage), the multi-artifact structure NeoForge later
collapsed; (2) the **game-patching half** that FML alone doesn't show: patches/ holds source
patches applied to decompiled Minecraft, producing the patched game + Forge API in src/ — the
'modify the game itself' strategy that complements runtime class transformation; and (3)
**SRG/MCP naming heritage** (MCPNamingService in fmlloader) versus NeoForge's move to Mojang
official mappings — the mapping-universe fault line that Omni's compat pipeline must
straddle for legacy-Forge-era mods.

Strategically, Forge is the second fork-governance data point after MultiMC: leadership
friction in 2023 split the ecosystem, NeoForge took the momentum (compare activity and the
26.x targeting in the fancymodloader dossier against this repo's cadence), and mods now target
NeoForge first. Same lesson, larger scale: community trust is an architectural asset.

## Architecture Components

### Multi-subproject FML (pre-consolidation)

- **Location**: `fmlloader/ + fmlcore/ + fmlearlydisplay/ + *language/`
- **Role**: The distributed layout NeoForge later collapsed into one FancyModLoader repo
- **Sources**: `layout`, `fml-loading`

Loader, core lifecycle, early display, and each language provider live as separate Gradle
subprojects with separate artifacts. Functionally these map one-to-one onto the consolidated
FancyModLoader packages (see that dossier); the delta is pure structure — and the successor's
choice to consolidate is the verdict on which structure won. Recorded as the 'before' picture
of the corpus's strongest consolidation case study.

### Game patch pipeline

- **Location**: `patches/ + src/ + minecraft.versions.toml`
- **Role**: Source-level patches to decompiled Minecraft produce the Forge-modified game
- **Sources**: `patches`

Beyond runtime class transformation, Forge rewrites the game: patches/ contains source diffs
applied to decompiled, deobfuscated Minecraft, producing a patched game with Forge's hook and
event surfaces baked in (src/). This is the deepest possible integration strategy — maximal
API power, maximal per-version porting cost — and the structural reason Forge-family updates
trail Fabric-family updates (quantified in the fabric-loader dossier's update-speed note).
OmniLoader's design explicitly avoids this cost curve: hooks via transformation, never via
maintained game patches.

### SRG/MCP naming service

- **Location**: `fmlloader/src/main/java/net/minecraftforge/fml/loading/MCPNamingService.java`
- **Role**: The legacy intermediate-mapping universe of the Forge era
- **Sources**: `mcp-naming`

Forge-era mods compile against SRG intermediate names (MCP heritage), remapped at runtime —
the third mapping universe in the corpus alongside Fabric's intermediary and NeoForge's Mojang
-official names. Any Omni compat support for the pre-NeoForge Forge back-catalog must translate
SRG; the tooling exists (the AutoRenamingTool lineage noted in the sinytra-connector dossier
handles SRG), but it is a distinct pipeline input Omni's Phase 3 mapping ADR must budget.

## Feature Inventory

### architecture

| Feature | Maturity | Future-proofing | Omni relevance | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baked-in game API via source patches | core | 2/5 | avoid | `patches`, `forge-docs` |

**Baked-in game API via source patches** — The game itself is patched to host Forge's event/hook/registry surfaces.

*Omni notes*: Maximal power, maximal porting drag. Omni takes the Fabric-family lesson instead: minimal core + transformation-based hooks.

### compat

| Feature | Maturity | Future-proofing | Omni relevance | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SRG mapping universe (legacy back-catalog) | legacy | 2/5 | observe | `mcp-naming` |

**SRG mapping universe (legacy back-catalog)** — The Forge-era intermediate naming scheme that a decade of mods compiled against.

*Omni notes*: Only relevant if Omni's census (Phase 6) shows meaningful demand for pre-1.20 Forge mods; then the compat pipeline adds SRG translation.

### dev-experience

| Feature | Maturity | Future-proofing | Omni relevance | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| In-repo MDK distribution | core | 4/5 | adopt | `mdk` |

**In-repo MDK distribution** — The mod development kit ships from the loader's own repository, versioned together.

*Omni notes*: Loader and mod-dev tooling versioned as one unit — Omni's native-mod SDK should live in the monorepo the same way.

### governance

| Feature | Maturity | Future-proofing | Omni relevance | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fork-governance outcome (Forge -> NeoForge) | legacy | 1/5 | avoid | `layout`, `forge-docs` |

**Fork-governance outcome (Forge -> NeoForge)** — The 2023 leadership split moved ecosystem momentum wholesale to the fork.

*Omni notes*: Second data point with MultiMC->Prism: this ecosystem forks around governance failure regardless of technical merit. Feeds the same Omni openness strategy.

## Analysis Notes

### Scope note

Comparative baseline: shared FML architecture (discovery, module classloading ancestry,
mods.toml, language providers, early display) is documented authoritatively in the
fancymodloader dossier; this analysis records only what the pre-fork baseline uniquely
establishes — the multi-subproject 'before' picture, the game-patch pipeline, SRG heritage,
and the governance outcome. The metadata format here is mods.toml (META-INF/mods.toml) versus
NeoForge's renamed neoforge.mods.toml — a one-line but load-bearing compat detail for reading
each family's jars.

*Sources*: `layout`, `patches`, `mcp-naming`
